note: Separates intrinsic from extrinsic bias and organises evaluation by data, model and output level.
title: Bias in Large Language Models: Origin, Evaluation, and Mitigation
explain_beginner: Large language models, the AI systems behind chatbots and writing tools, tend to absorb biases from their training data and can make unfair decisions. This paper explains where these biases come from, how researchers can detect them, and what techniques can reduce them. Understanding this matters because biased AI affects real people in critical areas like healthcare and the criminal justice system, so building fairer AI requires knowing how to spot and fix these problems.
explain_business: Organizations deploying language models in high-stakes domains face legal and reputational risks from algorithmic bias. This paper provides a structured framework for identifying where bias enters systems and which interventions work best at different stages. For executives, it clarifies that bias management requires investment across the entire pipeline, from data curation through post-deployment monitoring. Selecting appropriate mitigation strategies now prevents costly failures and regulatory issues later while building customer trust in AI-driven decisions.
explain_practitioner: This review categorizes bias in LLMs as intrinsic, originating from training data and model architecture, or extrinsic, arising from deployment context. The authors systematize evaluation approaches across three levels: examining training data for problematic patterns, analyzing model weights and behaviors, and assessing final outputs for discriminatory results. They survey mitigation techniques applied before training, during training, and after deployment, evaluating each approach's strengths and limitations to guide practitioners selecting appropriate interventions for their specific bias concerns.
